title: Can China Burn Away Indonesia’s Waste Crisis?
gist: Indonesia's landfill system is failing (Bantar Gebang collapse, only 32% of 37.3Mt waste managed in 2024, most landfills near capacity by 2028), creating a large opening for waste-to-energy buildout in which Chinese firms are the central suppliers.

insights.claim: In March 2026 a 50-metre garbage wall collapsed after heavy rain at Jakarta's Bantar Gebang landfill, killing seven people; it was the fifth waste avalanche in the Jakarta metropolitan area in six months.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Repeated fatal landfill failures raise political urgency and the odds of fast-tracked waste infrastructure procurement in Indonesia.
insights.quote: The collapse is the fifth waste avalanche in the metropolitan area in six months.

insights.claim: Bantar Gebang, one of the world's largest landfills at 110 hectares, receives 8,000 tonnes of waste per day from a Jakarta metropolitan area of 42 million people.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Sizes the single largest feedstock pool for any Jakarta-area waste-to-energy project.

insights.claim: Indonesia generated 37.3 million tonnes of waste in 2024 but only 32% was managed, and nearly 200 of 514 jurisdictions do not report waste data.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Large unmanaged volume and poor data signal both a big addressable market and execution/data risk for waste-infrastructure investors.
insights.locator: The collapse exposed a wider failure

insights.claim: Indonesia's annual waste generation could reach 65 million tonnes, with daily volumes exceeding 140,000 tonnes.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Implies near-doubling of waste volumes versus 2024, supporting long-run demand for disposal and WtE capacity.
insights.locator: The collapse exposed a wider failure

insights.claim: Most of Indonesia's 70-plus landfills are poorly run: 63% still practise illegal open dumping and many have under three years of capacity left, with President Prabowo Subianto warning most could hit capacity by 2028.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: A 2028 capacity cliff is a hard policy deadline that should pull forward WtE contract awards and tenders.
insights.locator: Much goes to more than 70 landfills

insights.claim: Indonesia's rapid waste-to-energy expansion has Chinese firms at its centre, and the authors frame Chinese WtE as a 'product-market fit' for a regional (Southeast Asian) waste problem.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Watch Chinese WtE equipment makers and EPC contractors for Indonesian and broader Southeast Asian order wins; a geopolitical-commercial channel of Chinese influence.
insights.quote: is emerging as a “product-market fit” for a regional waste problem
